subtitle: My First Blog Post
body: Today I decided to start writing about my experience learning programming. When I first started learning Python, I found it difficult to understand how all the different pieces fit together. Variables, functions, loops, and classes each seemed simple on their own, but putting everything together into a real project was a completely different experience. Over time, I realized that the best way to learn is simply to build things and make mistakes along the way. Every project gives me a chance to practice something new, and even when something does not work, debugging helps me understand the language better. I am hoping that this blog will be a place where I can document what I learn and look back at how much I have improved.

subtitle: Learning Python
body: Python has been one of the most interesting programming languages for me to learn because it allows me to focus on solving problems without having to worry too much about complicated syntax. I have been learning about functions, lists, dictionaries, modules, and working with files. One of the things I particularly enjoy is being able to take a small idea and turn it into a working program relatively quickly. However, I have also discovered that writing code that works and writing code that is well organized are two very different things. As my projects become larger, I am starting to pay more attention to folder structure, reusable functions, naming conventions, and keeping different parts of an application separated.

subtitle: Building My First Blog
body: I recently started building a simple blog application using Flask and Jinja. At first, the project seemed fairly straightforward because all I needed was a few pages and some blog posts. Once I started putting everything together, I realized that there are many small details involved in building even a simple web application. I needed to understand how routes work, how information is passed from Python to an HTML template, and how Jinja can dynamically generate pages. I also wanted to keep my data separate from my application code, so I decided to store my blog posts in a JSON file. This makes the project easier to understand and gives me a good introduction to the way real applications separate data from their logic.

subtitle: Why I Like Building Projects
body: One of the biggest lessons I have learned while studying computer science is that completing exercises is very different from building an actual project. A programming exercise usually tells you exactly what problem you need to solve, while a project often starts with only a general idea. You have to decide what technologies to use, how to organize your files, what data structures make sense, and how different components should communicate with each other. I think this uncertainty is what makes projects both frustrating and rewarding. When something finally works after spending an hour trying to figure out what went wrong, it feels much more satisfying than simply completing a small coding exercise.

subtitle: What I Want to Learn Next
body: There are still many areas of programming that I want to explore. I would like to become more comfortable with backend development and learn how larger applications are designed. I also want to improve my understanding of databases, APIs, authentication, and deployment. Eventually, I would like to build applications that are more than just small projects running on my computer. I think the best way to reach that goal is to continue building projects while gradually increasing their complexity. Instead of trying to learn everything at once, I want to focus on understanding the fundamentals and then use those fundamentals to create increasingly useful applications.
